teams.name: Brazil
teams.summary: Brazil have played at all nine Women's World Cups. They finished runners-up in 2007 and third in 1999, and Marta holds the record for most goals at a Women's World Cup with 17.

teams.name: United States
teams.summary: The most successful team in the tournament's history, with four titles (1991, 1999, 2015 and 2019). In 2023 they were knocked out by Sweden on penalties in the round of 16, their earliest exit.

teams.name: Germany
teams.summary: Two-time champions (2003 and 2007) and runners-up in 1995. They won the 2007 title without conceding a goal, but went out in the group stage in 2023 for the first time.

teams.name: Norway
teams.summary: Champions in 1995 and runners-up in the very first tournament in 1991. They also reached the semi-finals in 1999 and 2007, but were eliminated in the group stage in 2023.

teams.name: Japan
teams.summary: Champions in 2011, becoming the first Asian team to win a senior FIFA World Cup, after beating the United States on penalties in the final. Runners-up in 2015 and quarter-finalists in 2023.

teams.name: Spain
teams.summary: Spain first qualified in 2015 and became world champions in 2023 in only their third appearance, beating England 1-0 in the final.
